overview: Before anyone reaches for a full graphics screen just to show a number, there's the 7-segment display: seven individual LED bars (plus often a decimal point) arranged to form digits 0-9 and a few crude letters by lighting the right combination. Each segment is wired and controlled individually — there's no built-in driver chip — so displaying a digit means turning on several GPIO pins in the right pattern, and a multi-digit display (common in 4-digit clock modules) needs a technique called multiplexing to control many digits with a manageable number of pins, since driving each digit's segments individually and continuously would need far too many pins otherwise.
simpleSummary: Seven LED bars arranged to display any digit 0-9.

specifications.operatingVoltage: Each segment is a standard LED, ~2V forward voltage, needs a current-limiting resistor
specifications.configuration: Common-cathode or common-anode (determines whether segments are activated by sourcing or sinking current)
specifications.segmentCount: 7 segments (A-G) plus often a decimal point (DP)
specifications.multiplexing: Multi-digit modules share segment lines across digits, cycling through digits rapidly to appear simultaneously lit

pinMap.name: COM
pinMap.function: Common pin — ground (common-cathode) or power (common-anode) shared by all segments in one digit.
pinMap.currentLimit: Sum of all lit segments' current
pinMap.gotcha: Wiring a common-cathode display as if it were common-anode (or vice versa) means every segment appears inverted — always check which type you have before wiring.

useCases.title: Digital clock/timer display
useCases.scenario: Multiplexed multi-digit display showing time or countdown values.

useCases.title: Simple numeric readout
useCases.scenario: Show a single sensor value or counter without needing a full graphics display.

useCases.title: Scoreboard/counter display
